prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not prescribe centrally acting anticholinergics (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) in older adults or in any patient with cognitive impairment
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with right-hand rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; the response to levodopa may add a supportive criterion [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months, measuring lying and standing blood pressure at each step on metoprolol [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]

Treat the depression actively (review the fluoxetine dose and response, offer psychological therapy; avoid adding an MAO-B inhibitor to fluoxetine), and follow the cognitive complaint with repeat cognitive assessment, since MoCA 24/30 with independent daily function is not dementia
Refer for physiotherapy for turning, gait and balance, and for speech and language therapy for the hypophonia

patient.history_present_illness:
Mrs. Ortega is a 68-year-old right-handed retired university professor who presents to the outpatient neurology clinic for evaluation of tremor and slowed movements over the past 20 months. She was referred by her primary care physician after reporting a progressive worsening of motor symptoms that have begun to interfere with her daily activities.

Approximately 20 months ago, the patient developed an intermittent resting tremor in her right hand, appearing primarily when she was seated and relaxed and diminishing when she reached for objects. Around the same time, her daughter observed that she was moving more slowly than usual, taking longer to complete routine tasks such as dressing, cooking, and writing. About a year ago, a similar but milder tremor appeared in the left hand. Over the past 8 months she has felt unsteady when turning quickly or navigating around furniture, without vertigo, light-headedness or falls.

The patient also reports increasing difficulty with handwriting over the past year. She has been working on a memoir and notes that her handwriting has become progressively smaller and more cramped, to the point where she can barely read her own notes. She has switched to typing on a computer but finds that her fingers feel stiff and clumsy on the keyboard as well. Buttoning clothes and fastening jewelry have become increasingly difficult, particularly with the right hand.

Additionally, she reports insomnia with difficulty initiating sleep over the past several months, which she attributes to her depressed mood. Her daughter has noticed that her mother's voice has become softer and that she seems less emotionally expressive, with a more mask-like facial appearance. The patient acknowledges feeling depressed and reports a general decline in her memory, particularly for recent events, though she continues to manage her finances and medications independently.

She reports urinary frequency and occasional urgency but denies frank incontinence. She denies hallucinations, vivid dreams, or acting out dreams during sleep. She denies difficulty swallowing or excessive drooling. She denies any exposure to antipsychotic medications, metoclopramide, or other dopamine-blocking agents. There has been no history of encephalitis, significant head trauma, or exposure to environmental toxins.

neurological_exam.additional: Resting tremor of the right hand at approximately 4-5 Hz with a pill-rolling quality, and a milder intermittent rest tremor of the left hand. The tremor re-emerges after a brief latency with posture holding and is suppressed with intentional movement. No action tremor. No dystonia or chorea. Handwriting sample demonstrates progressive micrographia. Glabellar tap sign positive with failure to habituate. Orthostatic vital signs: supine BP 148/88 with HR 64, standing BP 140/84 with HR 70 after 3 minutes.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing without dysmetria bilaterally. Rapid alternating movements show progressive decrement in speed and amplitude, right more than left. Heel-to-shin testing intact bilaterally without ataxia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light (3 mm to 2 mm bilaterally). Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. No vertical gaze palsy. Facial sensation intact bilaterally. Marked hypomimia with reduced spontaneous blinking rate. Facial movements symmetric but diminished in amplitude. Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations or atrophy.
neurological_exam.gait: Narrow-based gait with stooped posture and reduced arm swing, the right arm nearly immobile during ambulation. Shortened stride length with mild shuffling. Turns require 5-6 steps (en bloc turning). Pull test: two steps of retropulsion, recovers unaided. No festination or freezing. Tandem gait mildly impaired. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech is mildly hypophonic with reduced prosody but remains fluent without paraphasic errors. Naming, repetition, and comprehension intact. Montreal Cognitive Assessment score 24/30, with points lost on trail-making (1 point), cube copy (1 point), clock drawing (1 point), phonemic fluency (1 point) and delayed recall (2 points). Affect is mildly blunted. No evidence of hallucinations or delusions on questioning.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk normal throughout. Marked bradykinesia with decrement on finger tapping, hand opening-closing, and pronation-supination on the right, mild on the left. Cogwheel rigidity at the right wrist and elbow, mild rigidity at the left wrist, augmented with contralateral activation. Lower extremity tone mildly increased, right more than left. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. No pronator drift. No pyramidal signs.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch and pinprick intact in all extremities. Proprioception intact at bilateral great toes. Vibration sense mildly reduced at bilateral ankles, likely age-related. No cortical sensory deficits.
